newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: U.N. urges Afghan factions to stop fighting.
newsitem.headline: U.N. urges Afghan factions to stop fighting.

text.p: The United Nations urged warring factions in Afghanistan on Monday to bring an immediate halt to aerial bombing of civilian targets, cease all hostilities and begin genuine peace talks.

The U.N. Special Mission to Afghanistan (UNSMA), in a statement issued in Islamabad, expressed "grave concern" over increase in hostilities in recent weeks amid stepped up peace efforts by UNSMA and some counrties.

"Particularly alarming is the resumption, in the last 48 hours, of the indiscriminate bombing of civilian targets in Kabul and elsewhere, killing several innocent Afghans and injuring many more," it said.

An opposition jet bombed a Kabul suburb on Sunday where witnesses said at least seven people were killed and 12 wounded, hours after opposition forces recaptured the Parawan province capital Charikar, north of Kabul, from the Taleban militia.

The U.N. statement said that in the last six months all aerial bombing of civilian areas had stopped after the opposition Supreme Council for the Defence of Afghanistan agreed to Special Mission head Norbert Holl to stop "this senseless and militarily purposeless form of hostilities".

"The resumption of this bombing in Kabul at this time -- and indeed at any time -- is most regrettable and deplorable," the statement said. "It simply complicates the already difficult search for peace in Afghanistan.

"The United Nations, therefore, earnestly appeals for the immediate halt of this aerial bombing of the civilian targets, and urges the warring parties in Afghanistan to cease all forms of hostilities, and to begin genuine negotiations for a lasting settlement, as called for again recently by the United Nations Security Council."
The latest opposition offensives north of Kabul has overshadowed efforts by Holl and neighbouring Pakistan for an intra-Afghan dialogue for the establishment of a broad-based government.
On Monday, Taleban forces were preparing for a counter-offensive.

A senior Pakistan Foreign Ministry official, Iftikhar Murshed, who has been shuttling between Afghan factions in recent weeks, held more talks with Taleban officials on Monday at Taleban's headquarters in the southern Afghan town of Kandahar, the official APP news agency said.
